title: An affine morphism with surjective structure map is a closed immersion
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] which is affine [pqf-def-affine-morphism], and let $f^\sharp:\mathcal O_Y\to f_*\mathcal O_X$ be the map of sheaves of rings on $Y$ given by $f$. If for every $y\in Y$ the induced map on stalks $\mathcal O_{Y,y}\to(f_*\mathcal O_X)_y$ is surjective, then $f$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion].

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma Tag 01QO (label lemma-closed-immersion, (3) implies (1)) together with Lemma Tag 01SA (label lemma-affine-equivalence-algebras); used in the last sentence of the proof of Descent, Lemma Tag 02L6

proof.text: View $f^\sharp:\mathcal O_Y\to f_*\mathcal O_X$ as a morphism of sheaves of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules on $Y$. The assumed surjectivity of every stalk map is equivalent, by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-surjective-iff-stalks] (applied to the underlying presheaves of sets), to local surjectivity: for every open $W\subseteq Y$ every section of $(f_*\mathcal O_X)(W)$ is, near each point of $W$, in the image of $f^\sharp$. Hence the subsheaf $\operatorname{Im}f^\sharp\subseteq f_*\mathcal O_X$ of local sections locally in the image of $f^\sharp$ is all of $f_*\mathcal O_X$. Since $f$ is affine, $f_*\mathcal O_X$ is a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_Y$-module by [lem-pc-affine-morphism-hi] (applied to the quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal O_X$), and $\mathcal O_Y$ is quasi-coherent. So [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-cokernel-image], part (3), applied to $\varphi=f^\sharp$, gives for every affine open $V\subseteq Y$: $(f_*\mathcal O_X)(V)=(\operatorname{Im}f^\sharp)(V)=f^\sharp_V(\mathcal O_Y(V))$, i.e. the ring map $\mathcal O_Y(V)\to\mathcal O_X(f^{-1}(V))=(f_*\mathcal O_X)(V)$ is surjective. (Local surjectivity alone does not give surjectivity on sections; quasi-coherence of $f_*\mathcal O_X$ is what is used here.)

source.place: Sheaves, Definition Tag 007U (surjective sheaf map) and Lemma Tag 0H7H (surjectivity detected on stalks)

proof.text: Because $f$ is affine, the inverse image $f^{-1}(V)$ of every affine open $V\subseteq Y$ is affine by [pqf-def-affine-morphism]. Combining this with Step 1 gives an affine-open covering of $Y$ for which the induced map on rings of sections is surjective.

Apply the converse affine-cover criterion in [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-affine-cover-criterion], which is the implication (3)\Rightarrow(1) of Morphisms Lemma Tag 01QO: a morphism whose inverse images of an affine open cover are affine and whose maps on rings of sections are surjective is a closed immersion. Therefore $f$ is a closed immersion.
